description: jsprit is an open-source Java toolkit for solving rich travelling salesman and vehicle routing problems with a single general-purpose metaheuristic (ruin and recreate). Its README lists capacitated, multiple-depot, time-window, backhaul, pickup-and-delivery, heterogeneous-fleet and time-dependent vehicle routing, the travelling salesman problem and dial-a-ride, and combinations of these; users define vehicles, vehicle types with capacity dimensions, jobs and constraints in code and can modify the algorithm and plot solutions. The project is maintained by GraphHopper, requires Java 21 or later and is distributed as source code on GitHub and as a package on Maven Central (jsprit-core release 2.0.0, published March 2026). It is location-independent and works for any road network worldwide. It is released under the Apache License 2.0 and is free to use. Caveats: jsprit is a library, not an application, so distances and travel times must come from a routing engine or cost matrix supplied by the user, and it optimises tours for a given demand, not simulating traffic. In infrastructure work it plans freight, delivery, waste collection and service tours, and it is the vehicle routing engine used with MATSim, for example to plan Berlin waste collection tours when assessing the electrification of collection fleets. Related records are MATSim and the VROOM route optimisation engine.
